name: Null Meridian Day — The Great Feed Silence, 2201
creator: The Unclocked (decentralized BCI-refuser collective)
description: On February 7, 2201, an estimated 800,000 Meridian 88 residents simultaneously disconnected from all neural feeds for exactly twenty-four hours in a coordinated action organized by The Unclocked collective through physical pamphlet distribution and analog radio. The silence — measurable as a 19% drop in corporate neural feed revenue for that day — was the largest voluntary BCI withdrawal event ever recorded. Participants reported the day as disorienting, euphoric, grief-inducing, or terrifying in roughly equal measure.
medium: physical organization, analog radio, lived experience
cultural_impact: Null Meridian Day proved that coordinated mass BCI withdrawal was logistically possible and gave The Unclocked movement its first major public legitimacy; corponations responded by making neural feed subscription termination procedurally more difficult within 90 days.
controversy: Several Tier 4 and 5 residents who participated reported that their voluntary disconnection triggered automatic wellness checks and home visits from Axiom security contractors — raising serious questions about surveillance of BCI status.
story_hooks: The analog radio signal used to coordinate Null Meridian Day was traced to a transmitter in a Tier 3 building — one registered to an Axiom subsidiary.
A character discovers that they were the only person on their block who did not disconnect that day — and has no memory of why.

The corponation response to Null Meridian Day included a classified internal report estimating what a 72-hour mass disconnection would cost; the figures in that report suggest something about neural feed dependency that Axiom has never disclosed.
